# Incident Report — 2026-02-28 Traffic Capture

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.2.28.88 | Consistent source across all suspicious traffic |
| MAC | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.2.28.88` bound to this MAC |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (workgroup/domain identifier EASYAS123 / easyas123.tech) | NBNS name registration and DHCP hostname option from 10.2.28.88, same MAC |
| Logged-in user | brolf | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic from 10.2.28.88, realm EASYAS123.TECH |

The local subnet is 10.2.28.0/24, with 10.2.28.2 as the domain controller/gateway (NBNS local master browser "EASYAS123", also resolves as EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech via DNS).

## Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (NetSupport Manager remote-access tool abused as a commodity RAT).

**Attribution: behavioral, high-confidence.** No IDS/Suricata alert file was present in the evidence directory, so this is not signature-confirmed by an IDS product. However, the C2 traffic carries the exact, distinctive NetSupport protocol strings on the wire:
- Client request header: `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`
- Server response header: `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)`
- Protocol body keywords: `CMD=POLL`, `CMD=ENCD`, `ES=1`, `DATA=<encrypted blob>`

This is the standard NetSupport Manager/RAT check-in and encrypted-command protocol, transported over plaintext HTTP-like requests to `/fakeurl.htm` on TCP/443 (no TLS handshake on this port — a known NetSupport RAT C2 trait).

## Timeline / Behavior
- Capture spans 2026-02-28 23:55:06 to 2026-03-01 04:16:35 (~4.36 hours, 15,512 packets).
- First contact to the C2 IP occurs at t=44.9s into the capture (TCP SYN 10.2.28.88 → 45.131.214.85:443) — i.e., the implant was already present and beaconing almost from the start of the capture. No dropper, installer, or executable download to 10.2.28.88 is visible anywhere in this capture (no `.exe/.dll/.msi` objects in any HTTP transfer, confirmed via `--export-objects`), so the initial infection vector is outside the capture window.
- A single long-lived TCP stream (stream 40) stays open for the session, with 264 POST requests to `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm`, most 36 bytes (routine `CMD=POLL` heartbeats), a few larger (`CMD=ENCD` command/data exchanges up to 244 bytes), running roughly once per minute for the full ~4.3-hour duration — classic RAT beaconing/keepalive behavior.
- The C2 IP was contacted directly by IP literal; no DNS resolution for 45.131.214.85 appears anywhere in the capture, so no C2 domain can be grounded in this evidence.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | 45.131.214.85:443 | TCP stream 40, 10.2.28.88↔45.131.214.85, sustained ~44.9s–15682s |
| URL | http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm | 264 HTTP POST requests, `frame.number 10058` onward |
| Protocol markers | `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)`, `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` | Follow TCP stream 40 |

No malicious domain, no transferred malware file, and no file hash could be grounded in this capture — the only artifact exchanged over the C2 channel is the encrypted `DATA=` protocol payload inside the POST/response bodies, not a discrete delivered file.

## Benign Context (not indicators)
- login.microsoftonline.com, settings-win.data.microsoft.com, v10.events.data.microsoft.com, ctldl.windowsupdate.com, edge.microsoft.com, msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com, ecs.office.com, update.googleapis.com, ocsp.digicert.com, www.msftconnecttest.com, windows.msn.com/www.msn.com, mobile.events.data.microsoft.com, self.events.data.microsoft.com — standard Windows/Edge/Office telemetry, update, and CRL/OCSP traffic.
- wpad.easyas123.tech / wpad.mshome.net — routine WPAD proxy auto-discovery lookups (mostly unresolved), normal on an AD-joined Windows host.
- EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech, `_ldap._tcp...easyas123.tech`, Kerberos/LDAP/DCE-RPC/SMB2 traffic to 10.2.28.2 — normal domain controller authentication and directory traffic.
- acroipm2.adobe.com / armmf.adobe.com — Adobe update-check services.
- 23.64.147.24 (TLS SNI www.fmcsa.dot.gov) — legitimate user browsing to a U.S. government site.
- DHCP entry for MAC 00:e0:4c:68:08:00 ("brads-MBP") — a separate, unrelated device on the LAN, not the victim host.

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), logged in as user "brolf" on the easyas123.tech domain, was running a NetSupport RAT implant for the full duration of this capture, beaconing roughly every 60 seconds over a persistent TCP/443 connection to 45.131.214.85 using the tool's native `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` protocol disguised as HTTP POSTs to `/fakeurl.htm`. The capture does not contain the initial delivery/installation traffic, so the infection vector predates this capture window and cannot be determined from this evidence alone.
